verses.1: Balaam saw that it was pleasing to the LORD to bless Israel, so he did not go as before to meet the omens, but turned his face toward the desert.
verses.2: Balaam raised his eyes and saw Israel encamped by their tribes. The spirit of God came upon him.
verses.3: He took up his parable and said: This is the message of Balaam son of Beor, the message of the man whose eyes are open,
verses.4: the message of one who hears the words of God, who sees a vision from the Most High, whose eyes are unveiled.
verses.5: How beautiful are your tents, O Jacob, your dwellings, O Israel!
verses.6: Like valleys spreading wide, like gardens beside a river, like tents that the LORD has pitched, like cedars by the water.
verses.7: Water will flow from his buckets, and his seed will be in many waters. His king will rise above Agag, and his kingdom will be exalted.
verses.8: God brought him out of Egypt like a lion, like a lion's roar he devours his enemies, breaks their bones, and crushes their arrows.
verses.9: He lies down like a lion, like a lion cub. Who can rouse him? Blessed be those who bless you, and cursed be those who curse you.
verses.10: Balak was furious with Balaam, and he struck his hands together. Balak said to Balaam, "I called you to curse my enemies, and you have blessed them three times."
verses.11: "Now go back to your place," he said. "I had said I would honor you, but now the LORD has kept you from honor."
verses.12: Balaam said to Balak, "Did I not also speak to your messengers whom you sent to me, saying,"
verses.13: "If Balak were to give me his full house of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the word of the LORD, to do good or evil on my own. Whatever the LORD says, that I must speak."
verses.14: "Now I am going to my people. Come, I will give you a word about what this people will do to your people in the last days."
verses.15: He took up his parable and said: This is the message of Balaam son of Beor, the message of the man whose eyes are open,
verses.16: the message of one who hears the words of God, who knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees a vision from the Most High, whose eyes are unveiled.
verses.17: I see it, but not now. I behold it, but not near: a star shall rise from Jacob, and a scepter shall rise from Israel. It shall crush the foreheads of Moab and shatter the sons of Seth.
verses.18: Edom shall be possessed, and Seir shall be possessed by his enemies, but Israel shall do valiantly.
verses.19: One shall come out of Jacob and destroy the remnant from the city.
verses.20: He saw Amalek and took up his parable, saying: Amalek was the first of the nations, but their end shall be eternal destruction.
verses.21: He saw the Kenites and took up his parable, saying: Strong is your dwelling, O Kenite, and you set your nest among the rocks.
verses.22: If only your dwelling were secure and your nest high on the rock! But if calamity comes upon you, then Assyria shall carry you off.
verses.23: He took up his parable and said: Alas, who will live when God does this?
verses.24: Ships shall come from the hands of Kittim, and they shall strike Assyria. They shall strike Eber, and they too shall be eternally destroyed.
verses.25: Balaam rose and went, returning to his place. Balak also went his way.

notes:
Notes
- v. 17: "star" (כּוֹכָב) and "scepter" (שֵׁבֶט) are symbolic of a future ruler or messianic figure; "Agag" refers to the king of Amalek.
- v. 24: "Kittim" (כִּתִּים) is a reference to a distant maritime nation, often associated with the Greeks in later tradition.
- v. 24: "Eber" (עֵבֶר) is a generic term for distant peoples, not necessarily the tribe of Hivites.

[2] Balaam raised his eyes and saw Israel encamped by their tribes. The spirit of God came upon him.

[3] He took up his parable and said: This is the message of Balaam son of Beor, the message of the man whose eyes are open,

[4] the message of one who hears the words of God, who sees a vision from the Most High, whose eyes are unveiled.

[5] How beautiful are your tents, O Jacob, your dwellings, O Israel!

[6] Like valleys spreading wide, like gardens beside a river, like tents that the LORD has pitched, like cedars by the water.

[7] Water will flow from his buckets, and his seed will be in many waters. His king will rise above Agag, and his kingdom will be exalted.

[8] God brought him out of Egypt like a lion, like a lion's roar he devours his enemies, breaks their bones, and crushes their arrows.

[9] He lies down like a lion, like a lion cub. Who can rouse him? Blessed be those who bless you, and cursed be those who curse you.

[10] Balak was furious with Balaam, and he struck his hands together. Balak said to Balaam, "I called you to curse my enemies, and you have blessed them three times."

[11] "Now go back to your place," he said. "I had said I would honor you, but now the LORD has kept you from honor."

[12] Balaam said to Balak, "Did I not also speak to your messengers whom you sent to me, saying,"

[13] "If Balak were to give me his full house of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the word of the LORD, to do good or evil on my own. Whatever the LORD says, that I must speak."

[14] "Now I am going to my people. Come, I will give you a word about what this people will do to your people in the last days."

[15] He took up his parable and said: This is the message of Balaam son of Beor, the message of the man whose eyes are open,

[16] the message of one who hears the words of God, who knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees a vision from the Most High, whose eyes are unveiled.

[17] I see it, but not now. I behold it, but not near: a star shall rise from Jacob, and a scepter shall rise from Israel. It shall crush the foreheads of Moab and shatter the sons of Seth.

[18] Edom shall be possessed, and Seir shall be possessed by his enemies, but Israel shall do valiantly.

[20] He saw Amalek and took up his parable, saying: Amalek was the first of the nations, but their end shall be eternal destruction.

[21] He saw the Kenites and took up his parable, saying: Strong is your dwelling, O Kenite, and you set your nest among the rocks.

[22] If only your dwelling were secure and your nest high on the rock! But if calamity comes upon you, then Assyria shall carry you off.

[23] He took up his parable and said: Alas, who will live when God does this?

[24] Ships shall come from the hands of Kittim, and they shall strike Assyria. They shall strike Eber, and they too shall be eternally destroyed.

[25] Balaam rose and went, returning to his place. Balak also went his way.

- v. 17: "star" (כּוֹכָב) and "scepter" (שֵׁבֶט) are symbolic of a future ruler or messianic figure; "Agag" refers to the king of Amalek.
- v. 24: "Kittim" (כִּתִּים) is a reference to a distant maritime nation, often associated with the Greeks in later tradition.
